title: introduce validate_mode + stream checkpoints to improve JSON schema enforcement and streaming recovery
author: Maya Kline
description:
Context & motivation: Customers running structured-output in production reported two classes of failures: (1) transient stream corruption during long-running streaming responses (partial JSON fragments that never reconcile), and (2) silent schema regressions when developers rely on soft validation. This PR introduces a small-but-impactful API surface + runtime changes to reduce both failure modes and to make OpenAI-compatible tool/function calling safer across streams.

What this change does (single sentence): Adds a validate_mode api option (off|warn|enforce) and a lightweight stream checkpointing protocol to enable resumable/repairable JSON-schema streaming with clearer error semantics and actionable telemetry.

Details (single continuous description): The new request-level parameter response_format.validate_mode controls runtime validation behavior. Mode semantics: 
- off: no validation at runtime (existing behavior).
- warn: runtime performs schema checks on streaming checkpoints and emits structured warnings in telemetry and the final response metadata; the model output is not rejected.
- enforce: runtime will attempt incremental correction using the last successful checkpoint, and if unrecoverable will terminate the stream early with a structured schema error payload (contract: status=invalid_schema, hint, checkpoint_cursor).

To support enforce/warn we introduce a compact checkpointing marker inserted into streaming chunks by the runtime when response_format.type == "json_schema" (configurable opt-in). Checkpoints are lightweight serialized deltas (SHA256 prefix + length + truncated fragment) and are never persisted to disk — they live in process in the serving worker's KV cache for up to 30s by default. On detection of parse failure the worker will rewind the stream to the last checkpoint and attempt one of: request a model retry (up to 2 attempts), coerce minor type mismatches (config-driven), or emit an enforce-mode structured error.

OpenAI-compat updates: function_call payloads in streaming now include an extra field function_call.arg_schema_hash to ensure tool arguments match expected schemas during incremental tool invocation. The compatibility shim will reject tool calls where arg_schema_hash != server-side registry hash unless validate_mode==off. This prevents silent mis-typed tool invocations observed during multi-stage streams.

Operational notes: Added telemetry tags response.validate_mode and stream.checkpoint_hit_count to Console so SRE can track enforcement rates and checkpoint efficacy. Default behavior remains warn for customers with response_format.schema specified; enforce must be enabled explicitly by the API client or via server-side policy on Dedicated/Private.

Checklist: 
- [x] API: add response_format.validate_mode to spec, update OpenAPI + TypeScript client generation. 
- [x] Runtime: implement checkpoint markers + rewind logic in serving worker. 
- [x] Compatibility: include arg_schema_hash in function_call shim and fallback mapping. 
- [x] Tests: unit + end-to-end streaming repro harness and integration against openai-compat mock. 
- [x] Docs: examples and migration guide added to redwood-docs (see related PR).

Backward compatibility and migration: validate_mode defaults to "warn" when response_format.schema is present to surface regressions without breaking running systems. Private/Dedicated customers can opt their clusters into enforce-by-default through a new cluster policy flag.

Risk & mitigations: enforce mode can cause early stream termination in presence of model hallucinations; mitigation: default to warn and expose retry budget + coercion toggles. We added a runtime metric for enforce-induced-terminations and a feature flag to turn off checkpoint insertion for latency-sensitive paths.

Related: This PR references a docs companion PR in redwood-docs and a small SDK change in redwood-sdk-python for the validate_mode parameter.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after two rounds of review and a flake rerun in streaming e2e tests.
commit_summary: add validate_mode enum to response_format and wire through OpenAPI spec
implement checkpointing markers and in-memory KV for streaming workers
add arg_schema_hash to function_call shim and check during tool call phase
integration tests: streaming-resume, schema-enforce and warn paths
update TS + Python clients to accept validate_mode and include examples
review_comments: Ethan Park: Can you clarify lifetime/size characteristics of checkpoints? We need bounds for SLO reasoning.
Author (Maya Kline): Checkpoints are bounded to 8KB truncated fragments + 8 byte prefix for the hash + metadata; retained in worker KV for 30s by default and configurable via cluster policy.
Priya Kapoor: I asked for clearer error payloads so clients can implement deterministic backoff. Please include a checkpoint_cursor and human-friendly hint in enforce failures.
Author (Maya Kline): Added checkpoint_cursor and a short hint field. Also included an example error JSON in the docs section.
Liam O'Neill: e2e streaming tests flaked due to timing on the mock model; please add a small jitter tolerance and rerun CI.
Author (Maya Kline): Increased test tolerance and added a retry wrapper. CI rerun passed. Approved by reviewers.
release_notes:
- Add response_format.validate_mode (off|warn|enforce) for runtime schema validation and clearer error semantics.
- Streaming checkpoint markers and rewind behavior to improve recovery from partial JSON fragments.
- function_call now carries arg_schema_hash to prevent silent tool-call schema mismatches.
- Telemetry: response.validate_mode and stream.checkpoint_hit_count added to Console.
notes_for_ops: Default _warn_ behaviour minimizes risk; enforce is opt-in. If you see a spike in enforce-induced-terminations after rollout, consider toggling cluster policy or increasing retry budget. Checkpoints are in-memory per-worker (30s) and do not affect disk persistence.
